name: Screen-sharing / remote-control app requested during a banking interaction
description: The recipient is asked to install a screen-sharing or remote-control app (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, AirDroid) in the context of a banking or payment interaction, letting an attacker watch the screen and drive the device. The signal is the screen-share app request combined with a banking/authority or payment context.

manual_retrieval.notes: Original HDFC page (SRC-008) is dead (D5). Current HDFC page explicitly names AnyDesk/TeamViewer/AirDroid as screen-sharing threats. INDUSTRY evidence corroborates but does not authorise; caps this rule at PARTIAL (ADR-0015).

explanation.plain: Someone helping you with a banking problem asked you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or a similar screen-sharing app. That lets them see your screen and control your phone while you bank. Your bank will never ask you to install one of these.
explanation.technical: SCREEN_SHARE_APP_REQUEST (device-action) with a banking/authority or payment context. Named on HDFC's current security page and corroborated by NPCI's remote-access warning.
verification_steps: Never install a screen-sharing app at the request of someone contacting you about your bank account.
If you already installed one, uninstall it and call your bank on the number on your card.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: The strongest available evidence is a commercial bank page (INDUSTRY), corroborated by NPCI's official remote-access warning. Held at PEER_REVIEW and capped at PARTIAL; a legitimate, user-initiated IT-support session (IT_SUPPORT_CONTEXT) suppresses it.

provenance.notes: UNSUPPORTED at Phase 1 (dead HDFC SRC-008, D5). Reconciled to the current HDFC page (SRC-026, MR-EVID-006) under DEC-006 / ADR-0015; INDUSTRY evidence, PARTIAL (capped). No manifest blocks_rules mapping was invented for SRC-026; the rule mapping is recorded in RESEARCH-004.
